title: From face-swap jokes to millions of plays

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fourteen million plays. That's the all-time total on Snapchat lenses that Antoine started making as a joke for friends in 2017.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: From a hobby. He used Lens Studio, which made face tracking and simple materials approachable, and shipped forty-two lenses between 2017 and 2020, for himself and for clients. The biggest, Go Crazy Facetime, passed about 2.9 million plays.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What changed from fun to a side business?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He noticed the metrics tab. After that, every release was a tiny product launch: a thumbnail, a preview video, one clear hook. Then Fiverr clients came along.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How did a client project work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four steps. A brief with a reference video, a quick prototype sent as a screen recording before any polish, review cycles, and delivery. He also kept a short checklist per lens: licensed audio, a thumbnail readable at phone size, effects triggering on the right part of the face, and a ten-second preview that shows the hook.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Smart. Plays and views are different, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. A lens can be opened once and watched several times, so he looks at both. Lifetime numbers are twenty million views, over seven hundred thousand shares and about 470 unique posters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A small utility that converts a GIF or video into PNG sequences, which Lens Studio wants for many effects. Batch export beats screenshotting frames by hand, and other Lens Studio creators picked it up too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They called him to collect Lens Studio feedback from active creators. He shared what he met daily, like load times, preview fidelity and documentation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He wants to explore Meta Spark for cross-platform AR.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lenses were his first taste of shipping creative work to millions of anonymous users with real analytics. Tight loops and testing on real devices carry over to everything else. The full page has the numbers and the tool link.
